extra_misconceptions.fact: Camera lenses concentrate sunlight onto the retina and can cause permanent blindness in a fraction of a second.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Looking at a solar eclipse through an optical camera viewfinder without a solar filter is safe for a second.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Warm indoor air condenses immediately on cold glass and electronics; seal the camera in a plastic bag so it warms slowly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bringing a freezing camera straight into a heated tent warms the battery safely without harming the lens.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Image files store embedded EXIF GPS coordinates by default unless location tagging is disabled or stripped before posting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Smartphone photos shared on social media never reveal the exact campsite coordinates where they were taken.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Carbon fiber conducts high-voltage lightning strikes, so photographers must pack gear and seek low shelter when thunder sounds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carbon-fiber tripods cannot conduct electricity and are safe to leave standing on an open ridge in a storm.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to walk backward while framing a subject through a viewfinder near ledges or roadways?
What happens to internal camera optics when cold winter gear is carried directly into a warm, humid cabin?
Which physical indicator warns you to pack away a tripod and move to shelter during approaching storms?
Where should a Scout check before posting camp photographs online to protect fellow Scouts' location privacy?

extra_misconceptions.fact: F-stops are fractions of focal length, so f/16 is a small opening while f/2.8 is a wide opening that admits much more light.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A larger f-stop number like f/16 represents a wider lens opening that lets more light reach the sensor.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Raising ISO amplifies the electronic signal after capture, which brightens the image while also amplifying digital noise.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Increasing the camera ISO physically makes the digital image sensor more sensitive to incoming photons.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Overhead midday sun casts harsh shadows under eyes and noses, whereas golden-hour or open-shade light wraps softly across faces.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Direct midday overhead sunlight produces the most flattering natural portraits with soft facial shadows.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The rule of thirds divides the frame with two horizontal and two vertical lines, placing subjects along those lines or intersections.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The rule of thirds requires placing the main subject dead center at the intersection of the middle frame.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to background blur and shutter speed when you stop a lens down from f/2.8 to f/16 in fixed light?
Under what condition does raising the ISO from 100 to 6400 degrade fine detail and color accuracy in shadows?
Where should a Scout position the horizon line using the rule of thirds when dramatic storm clouds fill the sky?
What shutter speed threshold freezes a running Scout cleanly versus deliberately blurring a cascading waterfall?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The adjustable aperture iris sits inside the lens barrel, while the mechanical shutter curtains sit inside the camera body.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The aperture diaphragm is housed inside the camera body right in front of the digital image sensor.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Half-pressing the shutter button activates the autofocus system and light meter without opening the shutter or recording a file.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pressing the shutter button halfway down begins recording a dim preliminary exposure onto the memory card.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Photodiodes measure only light intensity, so a Bayer red-green-blue filter mosaic sits over the sensor to reconstruct color.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Digital camera sensors capture full-color pixels directly without needing any color filter array over the silicon.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most mirrorless cameras still use a focal-plane mechanical shutter alongside an electronic shutter option to prevent rolling distortion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mirrorless cameras lack a mechanical shutter and can only expose images by turning the sensor on and off.

extra_socratic_questions: What sequence of mechanical and electronic actions occurs inside a camera body the instant you press the shutter?
What visual advantage does an electronic viewfinder offer over an optical mirror when previewing exposure settings?
Which camera component controls the physical diameter of the light beam passing through the lens elements?
What happens to the recorded image if the shutter curtains remain open longer than the exposure meter recommends?

extra_misconceptions.fact: True perspective changes only when you physically move the camera higher, lower, closer, or farther relative to the subject.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tilting the camera from the same standing spot counts as changing perspective in a comparative photo exercise.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Closing the aperture to f/16 reduces light significantly, requiring a slower shutter speed or higher ISO to match exposure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Switching from f/2.8 to f/16 keeps image brightness constant without any change to shutter speed or ISO.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Direct on-axis flash flattens facial depth with hard back shadows, while side window light creates soft directional modeling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: On-camera pop-up flash and window light produce the exact same shadow direction and color temperature.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Focusing closely on a nearby subject narrows depth of field dramatically even when the lens stays at the same aperture.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Depth of field depends solely on the f-stop number and is unaffected by camera-to-subject distance.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a subject's perceived stature when you shoot from ground level looking up versus eye level?
Which exposure setting must change to maintain identical brightness when you close the aperture by three stops?
Where should you place an off-camera flash relative to your subject to avoid flat, washed-out facial features?
What visual difference appears in the background when you step closer to your subject while keeping f/2.8 set?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Close wide-angle distances exaggerate the nose and shrink the ears; stepping back with an 85mm lens keeps features natural.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standing twelve inches from a person's face with a wide-angle lens produces the most natural close-up portrait.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Single-shot focus locks at one distance, whereas continuous autofocus (AF-C) updates focus constantly as the subject moves.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Single-shot autofocus (AF-S) is the best setting for capturing a bird in flight or a Scout crossing a finish line.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Direct flash startles wildlife and causes harsh eye reflections; raise ISO and use a fast lens with natural ambient light.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using a bright flash at close range is the safest way to highlight detail on wild animals at dusk.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Candid photographs capture unposed subjects absorbed in an activity without directing their posture or expression.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A candid photograph requires asking the subject to stop working and smile directly at the camera lens.

extra_socratic_questions: Which autofocus mode tracks a sprinting athlete or flying bird continuously across the frame before capture?
Where should the critical focus point rest when shooting a close-up portrait with a wide aperture like f/2?
What happens to facial proportions when you shoot a tight headshot inches away with a wide-angle 24mm lens?
Under what condition does panning the camera with a moving cyclist create a stronger action shot than high shutter speed?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Editing software can sharpen edges slightly, but it cannot recover optical focus or freeze motion that was blurred at capture.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Post-processing software can restore sharp detail to a severely motion-blurred or out-of-focus photograph.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every JPEG save applies lossy compression that degrades quality, so editors use non-destructive layers or keep master originals.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Saving and re-saving the original JPEG file repeatedly during editing preserves 100 percent of image quality.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Clipped JPEG highlights contain only maximum white values (255, 255, 255), so lowering brightness turns them flat gray.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Blown-out pure white highlights in a JPEG hold hidden cloud textures that return when you lower brightness.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excessive saturation clips color channels and causes unnatural neon skin tones and foliage; subtle vibrance adjustments preserve detail.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pushing the saturation slider to 100 percent makes outdoor nature photographs look more realistic and accurate.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to pixel resolution and print sharpness when you crop away eighty percent of an original image frame?
Which histogram indicator reveals that highlight detail in bright clouds is permanently clipped beyond recovery?
Why is it important to edit a non-destructive copy or RAW file instead of overwriting the original camera file?
What visual cast appears in an indoor photograph when the camera white balance stays set to daylight under tungsten bulbs?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 7 explicitly requires shooting new images dedicated to your planned event or topic rather than recycling earlier work.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reusing your best action and portrait photos from Requirements 4 and 5 satisfies the visual story requirement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Effective visual stories combine wide establishing shots, medium interaction frames, tight detail close-ups, and a closing image.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A strong photo essay consists of ten nearly identical eye-level medium shots of the main activity.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A pre-approved shot list ensures you capture key narrative stages, locations, and transitions even while reacting to candid action.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Planning a storyboard before an event is pointless because candid moments happen too fast to anticipate.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sequencing images by narrative flow, beginning, middle, climax, and resolution often communicates the story better than clock order.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Arranging story photographs in strict chronological timestamp order is always the only valid way to present them.

extra_socratic_questions: What role does a wide establishing shot play at the beginning of an eight-to-twelve-image visual story?
Why must a Scout obtain counselor approval on the shot list and storyboard before photographing the event?
Which mix of shot distances prevents a twelve-photo narrative from feeling repetitive to someone viewing it?
What criteria help you cull fifty event photos down to the ten strongest frames that advance the story arc?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Journalistic ethics strictly forbid adding, removing, or staging elements in news photos because accuracy and truth are mandatory.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A photojournalist is allowed to clone out distracting background objects to make a news photo cleaner.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most working photographers spend the majority of their time on client outreach, contracts, lighting setup, culling, and editing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Professional photographers spend nearly all of their working hours pressing the shutter button on location.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Clients hire photographers based on a cohesive portfolio, reliable lighting skill, and problem-solving under deadline pressure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Owning an expensive professional camera body automatically qualifies someone for commercial photography jobs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Forensic and scientific photographers follow strict scale, lighting, and color-calibration protocols so images serve as evidence.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Forensic and medical photographers focus on artistic expression rather than standardized technical documentation.

extra_socratic_questions: What ethical boundary separates a news photojournalist from a commercial advertising photographer during editing?
Which business and legal skills must a freelance photographer master beyond operating a camera and lighting rig?
Where can an aspiring photographer gain hands-on field mentorship before investing in commercial studio gear?
What portfolio qualities convince a photo editor or client to hire a specialist for a high-stakes assignment?
